To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have shown that markers of hemolysis, inflammation, and coagulation are associated with cognition, but not through blood flow velocity, in children with Sickle Cell Anemia (SCA) without stroke, and that hydroxyurea (HU) may be associated with higher cognition.

in addition to effects of maternal education, age and HU treatment, vasculopathic markers, such as LDH, ANC, TAT, and TF, are associated with cognitive performance in children with SICKLE CELL DISEASE without stroke.

in addition to effects of patient age and maternal education some vasculopathic biomarkers are associated with cognitive functioning in young children with sickle cell disease, and these relationships were not mediated by blood flow velocities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the cognitive function and the cerebral vasculopathy in children with Sickle Cell disease.
the development of a biomarker profile for cerebral vasculopathy in SCD and how this relates to cognitive function.
the identification of potential biomarkers of cerebrovascular disease and cognitive dysfunction in SCD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study provides preliminary evidence of the potential role of vasculopathic biomarkers in cognitive decline in children with Sickle Cell Anemia.

there is an urgent need for further research in this area, and that this study provides support for further study of the influence of vasulopathic markers on cognition in children with Sickle Cell disease.

vasculopathic markers, including blood flow velocities, are not independent predictors of IQ, but may be associated with cognitive function, and that maternal education and age are important independent predictors of cognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are not finding the expected relationships between biomarkers, blood flow velocity, and cognitive function.
the biomarkers we examined did not have a significant effect on the children's IQ scores.
there are few significant independent associations among biomarkers, blood flow velocity, and cognition in this sample.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we need more data to determine whether there is an association between cognitive function and vasculopathic markers in young children without stroke, and if so, whether this association is mediated through blood flow velocities.
there are multiple factors that may influence cognition in children with Sickle Cell Anemia, including vasculopathic markers, maternal education, and age.
there may be a relationship between LDH and cognitive function, and that this relationship may be independent of blood flow velocity.
